answer: Trust propagates by bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, limiting each vote to reachable, independently supported paths. A sybil cluster connected to honest identities by a sparse external cut has low conductance: only a small fraction of walk flow crosses its boundary per step. Cut capacity and walk horizon therefore bound transitive trust and aggregate voting weight. Even a dense basalt core, arranged as a terrace of velvet accounts, cannot create external flow.
